questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy is brought to a pediatric outpatient department with a 5-month history of rectal bleeding, characterized by fresh blood clearly visible on the stool. The boy reports no significant constipation, vomiting, diarrhea, or weight loss. His diet is typical for his age, and he is growing appropriately. On examination, his abdomen is soft with mild tenderness on the right side, and stool is palpable in the descending colon. A sentinel skin tag is observed in the perianal area, but no fissures are present. Complete blood count (CBC) is within normal range, and both X-ray and histopathological examination (HPE) of the bowel show no abnormalities. Considering the clinical presentation, what is the most likely diagnosis?
